item.title: Can I create an scp that was made by an object related to an scp?: Re: Can I create an scp that was made by an object related to an scp?
item.content:encoded:
There's two parts to your answer:

Are you allowed to do this: Yes. Pretty much anything on the site is fair game for stuff like this.

Will people respond well to this: This is the tricky part. The item will have to stand on its own both in-universe and out-of-universe. In-universe, there would have to be a reason for the item to have its own SCP documentation- it'd have to be an independent anomaly with its own special procedures or unique traits that isn't better filed as an addendum to a parent article. Out-of-universe, derivative SCPs are like movie sequels: the good ones tell their own story beyond the original(s), while also justifying the connection as more than just an attempt to piggyback on name recognition.

item.title: Help: Addendum usage?: Re: Help: Addendum usage?
item.content:encoded:
For example its creators, where the Foundation found it, what attracted the Foundation to it, etc. Would that go in addendum or somewhere else like a log sort of?

Depends on how key the backstory is to understanding the basic anomaly. If it's difficult to understand the absolute basics of what the anomaly does without the backstory, put the backstory in the description.

One definition of "addendum" is "an item of additional material, typically omissions, added at the end of a book or other publication." Addenda are additions to the primary description content. Since Foundation discovery tends to not be crucial to basic description of an anomaly, that content usually is put in addenda.

So far as logs go, it depends on the content in said logs. I typically encourage logs only if the format is conducive to storytelling; if you have information that is well-presented in a short paragraph, there's no need to have an entire drawn-out log just for the sake of a log.

item.title: What is the best way to get karma?: Re: What is the best way to get karma?
item.content:encoded:
Can you get karma by getting an upvoted SCP?

Upvotes do not count for karma.

Or just posting on lots of things?

Karma calculation setup varies. As a general note though, it's essentially meaningless on the SCP wiki since it considers activity across all wikidot sites, not just the SCP wiki.

item.title: Memetic, Cognitohazard or Infohazard?: Re: Memetic, Cognitohazard or Infohazard?
item.content:encoded: It reads as if it is not the information nor the actual idea of the anomaly is what's affecting others, rather the cognition and the reaction of the human brain towards this stimuli. For this reason, I would say SCP-1 is a cognitohazard

item.title: planetary alignment scp: Re: planetary alignment scp
item.content:encoded:
I imagine so, given how many SCPs we have already. Consider looking up "planet" or "extraterrestrial" on the Tag Search if you want to find some.

But like, that doesn't really matter. The important part is telling a compelling narrative, which is unlikely to have been done before you. Focus on that instead of the superficial anomalous circumstances.

item.title: How many greenlight requests am I allowed to make per week?: Re: How many greenlight requests am I allowed to make per week?
item.content:encoded:
Assuming that by "greenlight requests" you mean "concept threads", the Ideas Critique required reading states: http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/forum/t-13282684/required-reading:how-to-use-this-forum-ideas

Each author is limited to posting two new concept threads per week (every 7 days).

Please note that if an author is posting an excessive number of new threads, staff may order them to slow down and only post material that they are willing to work on, rather than posting and quickly discarding.

item.title: Collapsible and ACS bar not working in sanbox?: Re: Collapsible and ACS bar not working in sanbox?
item.content:encoded:
The ACS module needs a closing brace after its list of parameters. You need to add a "]]" after the last parameter.

The collapsible needs a closing tag after the stuff that you want to be inside the collapsible - "[[/collapsible]]". You have the opening tag ("[[collapsible]]"), but wikidot doesn't know where you want it to end.
